nodes.title: Powder Prompt List · Guide
widgets_values:
## 01 / Powder Prompt List

### Why use it
Prepare several descriptions to compare subjects or wording with the same model.

### How it works
Each enabled slot produces one prompt variant. Positive text describes what you want; negative text describes what to avoid. This node prepares text, not images.

### Inputs
Text entered in each slot or supplied through its input.

### Outputs
Aligned positive_prompts and negative_prompts lists.

### Example
Create red teapot and blue teapot slots. Connect positive_prompts to CLIP Text Encode, then to KSampler. Use a second encoder for the negative list.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Works without other Powder nodes. A prompt list causes downstream processing for each item; it is different from a latent batch.

### Practical tip
Disable unused slots. An enabled empty slot is still a prompt variant.

nodes.title: Powder Prompt Wildcard · Guide
widgets_values:
## 02 / Powder Prompt Wildcard

### Why use it
Run a sequence of descriptions without replacing the text before every Queue.

### How it works
Reads one prompt per line from the text field or a local file. count selects how many lines run together. Prefix and suffix add shared wording. Blank lines and # comments are skipped.

### Inputs
Prompt lines, optional file, start position and end-of-list policy.

### Outputs
Positive and negative prompt lists for this run.

### Example
Enter forest, city and coast on separate lines. With count=1, three Queue actions process them in order. Connect the outputs to standard CLIP Text Encode nodes.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Works without other Powder nodes.

### Practical tip
Stop blocks this branch at the end; Loop restarts it. Reset returns to the start. Repeat last holds the text selection, not the sampler seed.

Cursor progress is session-local. Browser reload/server restart starts a fresh cursor; Reset sets start_index to zero where available.

nodes.title: Powder Lora Loader · Guide
widgets_values:
## 03 / Powder Lora Loader

### Why use it
Apply LoRAs that change a model’s style, subject or details.

### How it works
Stack combines enabled LoRAs. Single tries them separately. The iteration order controls combinations with prompt variants. Duplicate LoRA rows keep independent strengths and triggers.

### Inputs
MODEL, CLIP, selected LoRAs and optional positive/negative prompt lists.

### Outputs
Patched MODEL/CLIP, prompt lists and lora_info metadata.

### Example
Checkpoint Loader → LoRA Loader. Connect MODEL to KSampler and CLIP to CLIP Text Encode. Connect lora_info to Powder Conditioner for automatic trigger assembly.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Weight loading works with standard nodes. Triggers travel separately in lora_info; standard CLIP Text Encode does not read it. Add trigger words manually when using that path.

### Practical tip
Use LoRAs made for your model family. Bypass LoRA CLIP skips only CLIP weights. Enabling a LoRA and enabling its trigger are separate controls.

Trigger edits are stored in the workflow; generation does not overwrite LoRA sidecar files.

nodes.title: Powder Styler · Guide
widgets_values:
## 04 / Powder Styler

### Why use it
Reuse visual style descriptions while keeping your main subject unchanged.

### How it works
Styles contain text before/after the subject and negative text. P/N controls each side. Sweep tries styles across runs; Repeat last holds the current selection.

### Inputs
Selected styles, enabled states, mixing strengths and optional sweep settings.

### Outputs
style: complete style settings; style_text: ordinary positive style text.

### Example
Send house by a lake to Conditioner.prompt and Styler.style to Conditioner.style. Change the style while keeping the house and lake.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Partly independent. Combine style_text with your subject for standard CLIP Text Encode. Full conditioning weights, placement and negative text require Powder Conditioner.

### Practical tip
style_text does not carry the entire style configuration. Text-only encoding does not reproduce cond mix weights.

Bundled styles currently contain positive suffix text only; negative/prefix controls apply when those fields are present in a style.

Cursor progress is session-local. Browser reload/server restart starts a fresh cursor; Reset sets start_index to zero where available.

nodes.title: Powder Canvas · Guide
widgets_values:
## 05 / Powder Canvas

### Why use it
Load a source image, work with layers and paint a mask. Layout separately describes object placement for supported models.

### How it works
Edit canvas changes the source. View results previews generated variants; accept one before it becomes the next source. Layout regions describe composition, not pixel-editing masks.

### Inputs
An image from a file or the image input, or a new blank canvas.

### Outputs
image, mask, batch_size and a layout description.

### Example
Canvas.image → VAE Encode; Canvas.mask → Set Latent Noise Mask; then KSampler → VAE Decode. Use Image Conditioning + Canvas Review for stitched edits with outside-area preservation (set stitch_blend=0 for the exact effective-mask boundary).

### Other Powder nodes required?
Image and mask outputs work with standard nodes. In-canvas result review uses Canvas Review. Layout is read by Conditioner; use Powder Sampler for model/size validation.

### Practical tip
Opening Layout does not enable its use: turn on Use layout. Reset All clears content and keeps the current tab. Enable Save mask in workflow and wait for saving before saving the workflow.

AI assistance and scene synchronization require qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors. Manual Layout editing does not.

nodes.title: Powder References · Guide
widgets_values:
## 06 / Powder References

### Why use it
Keep the source and extra reference pictures together so both sides of an edit refer to the same images.

### How it works
The bundle is shared by text and image conditioning. It does not edit an image or transfer a style on its own. Empty reference slots are skipped.

### Inputs
edited_image: the source being edited; image_1…image_4: additional references.

### Outputs
A POWDER_REFS bundle, not an ordinary IMAGE or LATENT.

### Example
Source → Image Conditioning.pixels and References.edited_image. Clothing reference → References.image_1. Connect the same bundle to Conditioner.references and Image Conditioning.references; use Edit.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Requires Powder consumers: Conditioner and Image Conditioning read this bundle. Standard KSampler and CLIP Text Encode do not accept it.

### Practical tip
The model must support reference editing. The edited_image field establishes text-side numbering; still connect the actual source to pixels.

nodes.title: Powder Image Conditioning · Guide
widgets_values:
## 07 / Powder Image Conditioning

### Why use it
Prepare an image, mask and model for generation or editing in one place.

### How it works
Generate starts from an empty latent. Repaint redraws the source. Repair works on a local crop around the mask. Edit uses model-specific reference conditioning. Denoise controls how freely the source can change.

### Inputs
Positive/negative conditioning, MODEL and VAE. Editing also uses pixels and mask. Generate can accept an existing empty latent.

### Outputs
Prepared positive, negative, latent, model, denoise and stitch context.

### Example
Load Image + CLIP Text Encode → Image Conditioning → standard KSampler. Wire model, positive, negative, latent and denoise. After VAE Decode, connect images and stitch to Canvas Review.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Generate and ordinary full-image img2img can use standard surrounding nodes. Returning a crop and preserving the outside image requires Powder Canvas Review. References are optional.

### Practical tip
An empty mask means the whole image. Low denoise preserves the source but may resist major changes; high denoise allows more change without guaranteeing the requested result.

Painted pixels retain the edit. stitch_blend adds an outside transition within the crop; use 0 for strict preservation outside the effective mask. mask_grow enlarges that mask.

Edit (native) keeps conditioning supplied by the model-specific encoder without adding Powder reference latents.

nodes.title: Powder Resolution · Guide
widgets_values:
## 08 / Powder Resolution

### Why use it
Choose output dimensions and the number of image variants.

### How it works
Preset selects a shape, Ratio uses your aspect ratio and target area, and Pixels uses explicit dimensions. The output is an empty latent for sampling, not a generated picture.

### Inputs
Size, batch count and latent format. Auto requires a connected MODEL; 3D image latents use one frame.

### Outputs
LATENT, width, height, a size string and a proportions preview.

### Example
Resolution.LATENT → KSampler.latent_image. For standard SDXL, choose SDXL/SD1 (4ch). All other nodes may be standard ComfyUI nodes.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Works without other Powder nodes. The preview shows proportions only.

### Practical tip
Match the latent format to the model. Dimensions may be snapped to the model grid; not every pixel size is representable.

nodes.title: Powder Conditioner · Guide
widgets_values:
## 09 / Powder Conditioner

### Why use it
Turn your description into conditioning understood by the image model, optionally combining styles and LoRA triggers.

### How it works
CLIP encodes the assembled text. Unchanged encodings can be cached. final_positive/final_negative show the actual descriptions used.

### Inputs
CLIP and prompt; optional negative_prompt, style, lora_info, references and layout.

### Outputs
Positive/negative CONDITIONING and the two final text strings.

### Example
Checkpoint Loader.CLIP → Conditioner.clip; your text → prompt. Connect positive_conditioning and negative_conditioning to standard KSampler.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Basic encoding works independently. Powder styles, trigger metadata, references and Layout are optional extensions. Layout requires a supported model and matching dimensions.

### Practical tip
Use the encoder that belongs to your image model. Inspect final_positive when a style or trigger seems to change the result unexpectedly.

Auto bypasses Flux/T5 and quantized encoders. CLIP hooks/schedules always encode fresh, including in Aggressive mode.

### Ideogram captions
Use a complete caption containing scene, style, background and objects. The Ideogram FULL template builds it from text using its local enhancer; LITE contains an editable JSON example. Conditioner keeps the structure and inserts styles and LoRA triggers inside it. Wrapping plain text alone does not fill missing object descriptions.

nodes.title: Powder Sampler · Guide
widgets_values:
## 10 / Powder Sampler

### Why use it
Generate an image latent from noise or a prepared source, guided by conditioning.

### How it works
Steps controls sampling work; CFG controls guidance; seed sets initial randomness; denoise controls redraw strength. Similarity blends noise across frames in the same batch.

### Inputs
MODEL, positive/negative conditioning, LATENT and sampling settings. Ideogram 4 also requires a compatible unconditional model.

### Outputs
A sampled latent. VAE Decode turns it into an image.

### Example
Checkpoint Loader + two CLIP Text Encode nodes + Empty Latent Image → Powder Sampler → VAE Decode → Save Image.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Works without other Powder nodes. Inpaint boost needs a noise mask already attached to the latent.

### Practical tip
Use a recipe appropriate to the model family. Scale steps by denoise changes the effective count. Fix seed and other settings when comparing results.

### Ideogram sampling
Standard keeps the existing schedule. First sigma +0.005 (experimental) changes only the first sampled sigma, keeping the step count and model weights. It can help with gray placeholders but may introduce artifacts. It is independent of Original / Enhanced in the prompt template. Compare using the same seed; other model families ignore this option.

nodes.title: Powder Inpaint Sampler · Guide
widgets_values:
## 11 / Powder Inpaint Sampler

### Why use it
Use mask refinement in a custom sampling chain with your own scheduler or guider.

### How it works
Selects an algorithm and boost profile but does not generate images itself. It supplies a SAMPLER component to SamplerCustom or SamplerCustomAdvanced.

### Inputs
Algorithm and inpaint boost level: off, soft, seams or max.

### Outputs
A SAMPLER object.

### Example
Powder Inpaint Sampler.SAMPLER → SamplerCustomAdvanced.sampler. Supply noise, guider, sigmas and latent through standard nodes.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Works without other Powder nodes. Its output does not connect directly to an ordinary KSampler.

### Practical tip
The latent must contain noise_mask for mask refinement. Stronger boost is not always better; compare boundaries and detail against off/soft at the same seed.

nodes.title: Powder Switcher · Guide
widgets_values:
## 12 / Powder Switcher

### Why use it
Choose an entire workflow branch with one selection, such as a matching MODEL, CLIP and VAE set.

### How it works
Groups are alternatives; channels are corresponding outputs. Exactly one group is active. Only the selected branch is requested for this switcher.

### Inputs
Alternative models, images, text, latents or other compatible values.

### Outputs
The channels of the active group.

### Example
Two Checkpoint Loaders → groups A/B with MODEL, CLIP and VAE channels. Switcher outputs feed standard encoding, sampling and decoding nodes.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Works without other Powder nodes. Selects values; it does not blend them.

### Practical tip
Keep corresponding channel types compatible. An empty selected channel blocks its consumers. A separate Save/Preview on another branch can still execute that branch independently.

nodes.title: Powder Canvas Review · Guide
widgets_values:
## 13 / Powder Canvas Review

### Why use it
Review generated images and, when needed, place an edited crop back into the original image.

### How it works
With stitch context, restores the crop using the saved source, mask and blending settings. Without stitch, passes images through and exposes previews. A connected Canvas can display them for acceptance.

### Inputs
Decoded images and optional stitch from Image Conditioning.

### Outputs
Final images for saving or comparison.

### Example
VAE Decode → Canvas Review.images; Image Conditioning.stitch → Canvas Review.stitch; Review.images → Save Image.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Plain review works independently. Stitching requires Image Conditioning; showing results inside the editor requires Canvas.

### Practical tip
Saving directly from VAE Decode bypasses stitching. Previewing a result does not automatically replace the Canvas source.

Painted pixels retain the edit. stitch_blend adds an outside transition within the crop; use 0 for strict preservation outside the effective mask. mask_grow enlarges that mask.

nodes.title: Powder Grid Saver · Guide
widgets_values:
## 14 / Powder Grid Saver

### Why use it
Save image variants together in a labeled comparison grid.

### How it works
Arranges images into rows/columns and optionally saves JSON parameters. It can also make a simple grid without Powder metadata.

### Inputs
Images; optional prompts, seed, lora_info and style_metadata.

### Outputs
grid_image and saved_paths. This node writes files.

### Example
Standard KSampler → VAE Decode → Grid Saver. Add lora_info from LoRA Loader for LoRA comparisons.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Works without other Powder nodes. Metadata improves labels but is not required to save a grid.

### Practical tip
Frames in one batch share a seed and have different batch indices. FULL templates initially bypass Grid; enable it when you want comparisons.

nodes.title: Powder Cache Stats · Guide
widgets_values:
## 15 / Powder Cache Stats

### Why use it
Inspect cached text encodings, raw LoRA files and loaded styles.

### How it works
Produces a diagnostic report without clearing data or generating images. Useful for checking reuse across repeated runs.

### Inputs
No inputs; execute the node.

### Outputs
A stats string and a short log summary.

### Example
Run a Powder workflow twice, then connect Cache Stats.stats to Preview Any and inspect cache sizes and hits.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Needs no connected Powder node, but reports this package’s caches rather than all ComfyUI memory.

### Practical tip
Entry counts are not GPU memory usage. Standard CLIP Text Encode does not use the Powder Conditioner cache.

Auto bypasses Flux/T5 and quantized encoders. CLIP hooks/schedules always encode fresh, including in Aggressive mode.

Produces a diagnostic report without clearing data or generating images. Useful for checking reuse across repeated runs.

### Inputs
No inputs; execute the node.

### Outputs
A stats string and a short log summary.

### Example
Run a Powder workflow twice, then connect Cache Stats.stats to Preview Any and inspect cache sizes and hits.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Needs no connected Powder node, but reports this package’s caches rather than all ComfyUI memory.

### Practical tip
Entry counts are not GPU memory usage. Standard CLIP Text Encode does not use the Powder Conditioner cache.

Auto bypasses Flux/T5 and quantized encoders. CLIP hooks/schedules always encode fresh, including in Aggressive mode.

nodes.title: Powder Clear Conditioning Cache · Guide
widgets_values:
## 16 / Powder Clear Conditioning Cache

### Why use it
Remove cached Powder Conditioner text encodings so they are computed again.

### How it works
A manual maintenance action. Does not delete images or unload every model from GPU memory.

### Inputs
trigger: change its value to request another execution.

### Outputs
No output ports. The log reports the number of cleared entries.

### Example
Change trigger, execute the cleanup separately, then run your generation workflow again.

### Other Powder nodes required?
Needs no connected node, but only affects Powder Conditioner’s cache. It does not clear standard encoders’ caches.

### Practical tip
Do not run it before every generation: that removes the benefit of caching. Repeating Queue with the same trigger may reuse the prior execution.

widgets_values:
# Independent nodes / required companions

Mix Powder and standard ComfyUI nodes freely where their port types match. The cards below explain independent tools, feature-specific dependencies and practical examples. Each arrow represents a connection between the named ports.

# Independent nodes / required companions

Mix Powder and standard ComfyUI nodes freely where their port types match. The cards below explain independent tools, feature-specific dependencies and practical examples. Each arrow represents a connection between the named ports.

nodes.title: 01 · Independent nodes
widgets_values:
## Use Powder inside a standard workflow

Independent means surrounded by normal ComfyUI nodes, not without required models and inputs.

- **Prompt List / Wildcard:** text → CLIP Text Encode.
- **LoRA Loader:** patched MODEL/CLIP → standard nodes; add triggers manually if not using Conditioner.
- **Canvas:** IMAGE/MASK → standard image-processing nodes.
- **Resolution:** LATENT → KSampler.
- **Conditioner:** CONDITIONING → KSampler.
- **Sampler:** LATENT → VAE Decode.
- **Inpaint Sampler:** SAMPLER → SamplerCustomAdvanced.
- **Switcher:** choose compatible branches.
- **Grid Saver:** IMAGE → saved grid.

Use only the tool you need. There is no requirement to replace your whole workflow.

nodes.title: 02 · Features that need a companion
widgets_values:
## Independent basics, connected advanced features

**Styler:** style_text works as ordinary text. Full style settings, conditioning weights and negative descriptions require Conditioner.

**Image Conditioning:** Generate and full-frame img2img work with standard sampling. Crop restoration and outside-area preservation (set stitch_blend=0 for the exact effective-mask boundary) use stitch → Canvas Review.

**Canvas Review:** reviews images alone. Stitching needs Image Conditioning; in-editor review needs Canvas.

**Canvas Layout:** layout is composition data, not a mask. Conditioner reads it; Powder Sampler checks model and dimensions.

**LoRA Loader:** weights work with standard nodes. Automatic trigger assembly uses lora_info → Conditioner.

nodes.title: 03 · Powder-specific bundles and utilities
widgets_values:
## What is tied to Powder

**References** outputs POWDER_REFS, consumed by Conditioner and Image Conditioning. Standard KSampler and CLIP Text Encode do not accept it.

**Cache Stats** reports Powder caches. **Clear Conditioning Cache** clears Powder Conditioner’s cache. Neither needs connecting wires, but neither controls every ComfyUI cache.

**Special connections:**
- References → references: shared reference set.
- Styler.style → Conditioner.style: full style settings.
- LoRA Loader.lora_info → Conditioner.lora_info: triggers; → Grid Saver.lora_info: labels.
- Image Conditioning.stitch → Canvas Review.stitch: restore the edited area.

Ordinary IMAGE, MASK, MODEL, CLIP, LATENT and CONDITIONING ports do not have this Powder-only restriction.

nodes.title: 04 · Example: one Powder node
widgets_values:
## Replace only the size control

Checkpoint Loader.MODEL → KSampler.model

Checkpoint Loader.CLIP → two CLIP Text Encode nodes → KSampler.positive / negative

**Powder Resolution.LATENT → KSampler.latent_image**

KSampler → VAE Decode → Save Image

Checkpoint Loader.VAE → VAE Decode.vae

For standard SDXL, choose SDXL/SD1 (4ch), start around 1024 pixels, and set batch_size=2 for two variants.

Resolution is the only Powder node in this example. You can similarly replace just the sampler or add a switcher.

nodes.title: 05 · Example: a local edit
widgets_values:
## Change an area and preserve the rest

Canvas.image → Image Conditioning.pixels
Canvas.mask → Image Conditioning.mask

Supply compatible MODEL, VAE and positive/negative conditioning. Choose Repaint or Repair.

Image Conditioning.model / positive / negative / latent / denoise → matching KSampler inputs

KSampler → VAE Decode → Canvas Review.images
**Image Conditioning.stitch → Canvas Review.stitch**
Canvas Review.images → Save Image

Mask the entire area you want to change. A teapot body-only mask keeps the original handle color.

A standard image/mask source can replace Canvas. Keep Image Conditioning + Canvas Review when you need stitching.

nodes.title: 06 · Example: styles and references
widgets_values:
## Two different kinds of guidance

**Text style:**
Subject → Conditioner.prompt
Styler.style → Conditioner.style
Conditioner → sampler → VAE Decode

Example: house by a lake + watercolor. This does not require References or an edit model.

**Image references:**
Source → Image Conditioning.pixels and References.edited_image
Extra image → References.image_1
References → Conditioner.references AND Image Conditioning.references
Conditioner → Image Conditioning (Edit) → sampler → VAE Decode → Canvas Review

Use a model that supports reference editing. The reference bundle cannot add that capability to an ordinary SDXL model. Text encoder requirements depend on the selected model.
